contentUpdates.oldStr: Recommendation: online-only for the pilot, but use UUIDs for primary keys anyway. Offline can then be added later without migrating every key.
contentUpdates.newStr: Decided 3 October 2026: online-only for the pilot. Sales go straight to the server, and primary keys are UUIDs from day one, so an offline queue can be added later without migrating a single key.

contentUpdates.oldStr: Recommendation: ship the flags, and ask the pilot pharmacy before building the register. The flags cost nothing now and prevent a migration later. Worth confirming against Pharmacy Council of Ghana and FDA requirements before the pilot goes live.
contentUpdates.newStr: Decided 3 October 2026: the register is required by law, so it is in v1. The Pharmacy Act 1994 (Act 489) s.34 requires anyone supplying Class A or B drugs to keep a Dangerous Drugs Record showing the drug and quantity, the name and address of the person supplied, the signature of the person supplying, and the date of supply; s.32 requires a dispensed prescription to be retained on the premises for two years. The FDA's controlled drugs guideline (FDA/DRI/TSA/GL-SSCS/2020/07 §4.3.1) requires a Controlled Drugs Register for everything obtained and supplied, kept and available for inspection for at least two years, and restricts pharmacy supply to a valid prescription or signed order. The register is therefore append-only, prescriptions carry a retained_until date, and controlled or prescription-only items cannot be sold without one. Sources: [Pharmacy Act 1994 (Act 489)](https://www.moh.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Pharmacy-Act-1994-Act-489.pdf) · [FDA — sale, supply and use of controlled drugs](https://fdaghana.gov.gh/final-guidelines-for-the-sale-supply-and-use-of-controlled-drugs-4/)
